status.en: 25 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 39% more than the week before, most of them in Tigray, Amhara and Addis Ababa.
status.nb: 25 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 39 prosent flere enn uken før, flest i Tigray, Amhara og Addis Ababa.

summary.en: Ethiopia has received 12 Russian Su-35 fighter jets and announced plans to acquire S-400 air defence systems while clashes have forced up to 50,000 people to flee across the Kenya border into Moyale County. Armed attackers killed at least 60 Orthodox Christians in Oromia and a drone strike killed two government civil servants in western Oromia. Senior Tigray Military Commander Major General Yohannes was captured near the Eritrean border. The UCDP recorded 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Etiopia har mottatt 12 russiske Su‑35 jagerfly og kunngjort planer om å anskaffe S‑400 luftforsvarssystemer, mens kamper har tvunget opptil 50 000 personer til å flykte over Kenyas grense til Moyale fylke. Bevæpnede angripere drepte minst 60 ortodokse kristne i Oromia, og et droneangrep drepte to sivile tjenestemenn i vestlige Oromia. Den senior tigray-militære kommandanten major general Yohannes ble fanget nær den eritreiske grensen. UCDP registrerte 2 824 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Fano insurgency
background.extract: The Fano insurgency is an armed conflict and insurgency in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia that began in April 2023 between the Fano militia and the Ethiopian government. The conflict started after the government attempted to dissolve the Amhara Special Forces and other regional forces as part of a plan to reform and centralize the country's security apparatus, and integrate them into the federal armed forces. This move led to protests and armed resistance by local forces under Fano.
